title.narrative: Tackling Trafficking and Crime along Corridors of Eastern and Southern Africa (TraCES Africa)

description.narrative: As Global Gateway investments gradually strengthen road, rail and port connectivity across the African continent, new opportunities for trade and regional integration are being created ¿ but so too are heightened risks of exploitation of these routes by organised crime and illicit trafficking networks. The development of strategic land corridors linking ports such as Mombasa, Durban and Lobito to the interior has made them both potential economic lifelines as well as vectors for organised crime. Across Eastern, Southern and Central Africa in particular, organised criminal networks exploit weak border governance, porous frontiers, corruption and uneven enforcement capacities, for trafficking in minerals, wildlife, fuel, firearms, illict drugs, human beings and migrant smuggling. These illicit flows move fluidly between legal and illegal economies, undermining state revenues, distorting markets and fuelling instability in fragile areas, also reaching EU Member States and affecting the EU¿s internal security. These trends call for a holistic, intelligence-led and corridor-based approach with an integral human dimension, rather than narrow, commodity-specific interventions.This Action responds to the growing security and governance challenges emerging along Africa¿s expanding trade and transport corridors, with the overall aim to reduce illicit trafficking and enhance security along key Global Gateway corridors through three interlinked outcomes:1.Enhanced intelligence through the establishment of National Intelligence Focal Points (NIFPs) and a Regional Intelligence Cell (RIC) to analyse, consolidate and disseminate corridor-specific risk profiles;2.Strengthened capacities for border posts, mobile enforcement teams and joint road-control operations, integrating an inclusive, gender-responsive and human rights-based (HRBA) approach;3.Regional cooperation and policy coherence: promotion and replication of good practices at regional level, supported by peer review and policy exchange.
